page: Amazon Web Services im4gn.xlarge is a storage-optimized server instance powered by an AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor. It features 4 dedicated physical ARM64 cores operating at 2.5 GHz with a single thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. A key feature of this instance is its bundled local storage, consisting of a 1875 GB NVMe SSD. Network performance is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 6 Gbps, and the instance runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the im4gn.xlarge delivers moderate CPU and memory capabilities. In stress-ng testing, both single-core and multi-core CPU performance fall within the average range. Memory bandwidth for large blocks also registers in the average tier, though small-block read-only memory bandwidth is weaker. The instance exhibits lower performance in compute-heavy tasks, with Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores, as well as Passmark CPU scores, landing in the weak to poor categories. However, it maintains average performance in Passmark database operations, reflecting its optimization for storage-centric workloads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the im4gn.xlarge offers a high density of local NVMe SSD storage relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for storage-bound workloads without the overhead of high-tier CPU pricing. Given its hardware profile and benchmark results, this instance is best suited for applications requiring high-capacity local storage and moderate compute, such as database operations, caching layers, and general-purpose storage-heavy tasks. It is less suited for intensive CPU-bound tasks, cryptography-heavy applications, or large language model inference.
